heroLead: Belle Vernon sits on the Monongahela right where Fayette and Westmoreland counties meet, river-town ground with a long industrial and mineral history.
intro: Belle Vernon grew up around glass and steel manufacturing, and like a lot of Mon Valley towns, the outlying farmland once tied to those industries often had its mineral rights split off long before anyone thought about shale gas. If your family holds an interest here, it may trace back through an old industrial-era deed as easily as a farm deed, and figuring out which one applies to your specific tract matters for confirming what you actually own.
We know how easy it is to lose track of a mineral interest across a family's move away from a river town like this one. We'll help you find the thread again.

sections.heading: River town, county-line complications
paragraphs: Because Belle Vernon sits near the Fayette-Westmoreland county line, it's worth double-checking exactly which county's records your specific tract falls under, since that determines where the deed is recorded and which courthouse holds your chain of title. We confirm this as one of the first steps in any title review here.
This area sits within the wet-gas Marcellus fairway, with the usual natural gas liquids processing deduction showing up on royalty statements tied to producing units nearby.

sections.heading: Old industrial deeds versus farm deeds
paragraphs: A tract that once supported a glass or steel operation may have a different chain of title than a straightforward family farm, sometimes involving a corporate owner at some point in the history. We trace whichever path applies to your specific parcel rather than assuming a single template fits every Belle Vernon deed.

sections.heading: Building an accurate offer
paragraphs: Once your specific county records and title chain are confirmed, we check current lease and production status and put together a number based on your actual documented interest.

faqs.answer: Yes, it determines where your deed is recorded and where we need to search. We confirm this early in the process so there's no confusion.
